title: Nocturnal North African Moroccan Lamb Mechoui
description: A rich and flavorful one-pot dish featuring tender lamb, crispy bread, and a tangy red wine jelly. Serve in a beautiful lacquerware bowl for a truly authentic Moroccan experience.

ingredients.name: Lamb shoulder (2 lbs)
ingredients.notes: Bone-in lamb shoulder works best for this recipe.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.notes: Use a high-quality extra-virgin olive oil.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Chopped onion adds a sweet and savory flavor.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Minced garlic is essential for Moroccan flavors.

ingredients.name: Red wine jelly
ingredients.notes: Homemade or store-bought, red wine jelly makes this dish pop.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.notes: A drizzle of honey balances out the tanginess.

ingredients.name: Cumin
ingredients.notes: Ground cumin is a staple in Moroccan cuisine.

ingredients.name: Paprika
ingredients.notes: Smoked paprika adds a smoky depth.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use kosher salt for a better texture.

ingredients.name: Bread
ingredients.notes: Cube the bread for crispy texture.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.notes: Chopped parsley adds freshness and color.

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.notes: A squeeze of lemon juice brightens up the flavors.

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large lacquerware bowl over medium-high heat.
Sear the lamb shoulder until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the lamb from the bowl and set aside.
Add the chopped onion to the bowl and cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Add the cumin, paprika, and salt to the bowl and stir to combine.
Return the lamb shoulder to the bowl and add the red wine jelly, honey, and lemon juice.
Braise the lamb in the bowl over low heat for about 2 hours, or until tender.
Cube the bread and toss with a little olive oil.
Spread the bread cubes on a baking sheet and toast in the oven until crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
To serve, place the braised lamb in the bowl and top with crispy bread, chopped parsley, and a dollop of red wine jelly.
